title: Prophylactic VacStent GI™ Placement After RAMIE – Proof of Concept Study
summary:
Anastomotic leakage is a serious complication that can occur after surgery to remove part of the esophagus. It happens when the connection between the esophagus and the stomach does not heal properly and develops a leak. This can lead to serious infections and other complications and may increase the risk of death. Even with modern surgical techniques, leaks occur in more than 10% of patients.

There are several ways to treat an anastomotic leak. Two commonly used treatments are metal stents, which cover the leak from the inside, and endoscopic vacuum therapy, which uses gentle suction to help the damaged area heal. A newer device, called the VacStent GI™, combines both approaches: it keeps the connection open like a stent while also using gentle vacuum therapy to support healing.

The aim of this study is to investigate whether placing the VacStent GI™ during surgery is safe and feasible in patients undergoing robot-assisted Ivor Lewis esophagectomy. The goal is to determine whether this preventive treatment may help reduce the risk of anastomotic leakage after surgery.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm: Lower third of oesophagus

interventions.name: Prophylactic VacStent GI™ placement following RAMIE in prospectively enrolled patients
RAMIE analyzed in a historical cohort

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Indications for elective RAMIE with intrathoracic esophagogastrostomy (Ivor-Lewis) 
• ASA I–III
• ECOG ≤ II
• Ability to understand the study’s content and scope and to comply with its requirements
• Verbal and written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Emergency surgeries, ASA IV, ECOG > II, participation in an interventional study that affects the outcome, and an impaired mental state that precludes participation
